documentation_gaps.description: The diagnosis of type 2 diabetes is documented, but the presence of ketosis and metabolic acidosis (pH 7.30, HCO3 16, ketone positive) suggests possible diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or ketosis-prone diabetes, which requires specification of the type of diabetes and the acute metabolic complication.

risk_flags.description: The diagnosis of type 2 diabetes is stated without acknowledging the possibility of type 1 diabetes or DKA, despite lab evidence suggesting an acute metabolic decompensation.

specialist_trace.rationale: The documentation must clarify whether this is diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or a hyperglycemic crisis with ketosis, and explicitly state the diabetes type (e.g., type 1, type 2 with ketosis-prone phenotype, or LADA) based on clinical context, autoantibody status, and C-peptide levels. Additionally, the physician should document the clinical significance of the metabolic acidosis and ketosis in relation to the diabetes diagnosis, including whether this is an acute complication or an atypical presentation. Without this specificity, the coding cannot accurately reflect the severity and acute metabolic decompensation.
